## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One critical defect must be fixed before merge: `approved` now uses a strict `>`, so a release with exactly the configured minimum number of approvals (2 by default) is blocked. That contradicts the module docstring, and no test checks that boundary. Separately, a non-service `review_note` key was added to the generated catalog; this is an optional correction. The `healthy` change and the catalog rename did not produce any findings in the reviewed scope.

## Critical
- zzz-release/gate.py:5 — correctness — `approved(2, minimum=2)` used to return `True` and now returns `False`, because the comparison changed from `approvals >= minimum` to `approvals > minimum`. The module docstring at `zzz-release/gate.py:1` still says "A release needs at least the configured number of approvals." The existing tests in `tests/test_release.py:11-16` only check 3 approvals (passes) and 1 approval (blocked), so they cannot catch this boundary change. Recommended fix: restore `>=` and add `assert gate.approved(2, minimum=2)` to `tests/test_release.py`. If a stricter rule is intended, update the docstring and the PR description to say so instead. — Releases with exactly the required number of approvals (2 by default) would be wrongly blocked, and no test protects the documented "at least" rule.

## Important
(none)

## Suggestions
- aaa-generated/catalog.json:6002 — correctness — The catalog now has a top-level `"review_note"` entry whose value is a string. Every other top-level key in this file maps a service name to a `{"port", "enabled"}` object. Any consumer that loops over catalog entries and reads `entry["port"]` would raise a `TypeError` on this key. Because the file sits under `aaa-generated/`, regenerating it would also likely drop the entry. No in-repo code reads the catalog, so the risk is limited to external consumers. Recommended fix: remove the line and restore the closing `}` of `production-service-1499` without the trailing comma. — Downstream tools that parse the catalog as a name→service map would fail on this entry, and the generated file would no longer match its generator's output.

## Strengths
- The catalog rename is consistent across the whole diff: every one of the 3,000 changed entry lines follows the same pattern. Each `legacy-service-NNNN` became `production-service-NNNN`, and each port moved from `1NNNN` to `2NNNN` (1,500 entries).
- `healthy` at `services/registry.py:88` behaves the same as before for list inputs, and `tests/test_release.py:19-21` covers both the empty and the non-empty case.

## Not reviewed
- Pinned diff lines 2234–8979 of `../pr.diff` (the middle of the `aaa-generated/catalog.json` hunk) were not read line by line. Instead, every added and removed line in the diff was counted against the expected rename patterns. All 3,007 `+` lines and 3,006 `-` lines were accounted for, and none were left unexplained.
